html:
A ship canal about 98 kilometres long across Schleswig Holstein in northern Germany, linking the North Sea with the Baltic. It was built from 1887 to 1895.

Before it, ships between the two seas had to sail all the way round Denmark, through stormy waters. Germany also wanted its navy to move quickly between its North Sea and Baltic ports. Thousands of workers dug the canal in eight years. Emperor Wilhelm II opened it in 1895, and it was first named the Kaiser Wilhelm Canal.

As Germany built ever larger battleships in the naval race with Britain, the canal was widened and deepened, with the work finished in 1914. After the First World War, the Treaty of Versailles opened it to ships of all nations. It is one of the busiest artificial waterways in the world by number of ships. Like the Suez Canal and the Corinth Canal, it belongs to an age when engineers cut new routes for steamships. It was begun under Wilhelm I, while Bismarck was still chancellor.
sum: A ship canal about 98 kilometres long across Schleswig Holstein in northern Germany, linking the North Sea with the Baltic. It was built from 1887 to 1895.
